paragraph_audit.reason: The title and agreement heading identify the document but impose no operative rule.
The paragraph defines the provider, platform, and user; these definitions provide context but do not themselves grant or restrict an activity.
The paragraph states when the agreement takes effect and that it applies to new platform features, products, and services, subject to the stated legal exception.
The listed registration and real-name authentication steps are represented as prerequisites to use.

The civil-capacity prerequisite is modeled, but the paragraph also states that an agreement may be void from the outset, permits the provider to stop service or cancel the account, and allocates losses and compensation. Those consequences cannot be faithfully represented with the supplied activities and modalities.

The paragraph defines registration and authorizes the provider to freeze or close accounts or refuse service for improper registration or use of multiple accounts, and states a compensation consequence. These provider actions and the liability allocation cannot be faithfully represented with the supplied activities and modalities.
Models the stated permission to log in using the user's set or confirmed phone number and set password; the remaining loss and recovery language is a liability allocation.
Captures the authorized transfer exception, process condition, transfer of account rights and obligations, and prohibition outside the exception.
Captures the ongoing update duty, legally conditioned verification cooperation duty, provider inquiry/recertification and suspension discretion, and listed factual circumstances.

Warranty/liability language and the statement that generated-content copyright is maintained by the user do not create additional grants or duties.
Heading and introductory statement that violations listed below constitute breach and may be handled; the specific operative handling measures appear in the following paragraph.
